sources_considered.why: A contemporary primary evaluation reports substantial success alongside important errors. Its narrow scope cannot establish reliability across generative AI.
A broad primary evaluation framework explains why reliability requires several measures. Its older results are methodological context.
Search results describe a narrow examination study spanning multiple periods, including testing after the post. It cannot establish the broad claim for the chosen target period.
The later visual experiments concern a different period and a selected task family.

evidence_items.explanation: The January report presents many positively scored ophthalmic answers while also documenting incorrect and potentially harmful answers. It qualifies a blanket inference from failures, but one medical task does not settle how common dependable performance is; the date identifies the report, not separately dated trials.

evidence_items.locator: Abstract, discussion of the multi-metric approach
evidence_items.explanation: HELM distinguishes accuracy from other relevant properties across multiple scenarios. It provides methodological context, but its earlier evaluation cannot establish the claimed frequency of reliable uses in January 2024.

unresolved_gaps: No representative estimate of the proportion of ordinary generative-AI uses meeting defensible reliability standards was established.
The claim does not identify a task population or a threshold for dependable performance.
The contemporary medical report does not separately date the underlying trials in the retrieved text.
